Global Foods Inc. - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Global Foods Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. Today's conference is being recorded. At this time, I would like to inform you that this call is being webcast live and can be accessed via the Investor Relations section of our website.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera (Vice President of Investor Relations):
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Global Foods Inc.'s Q3 2024 results. Joining me on the call are Michael Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Jenkins, Chief Financial Officer; and Lisa Chen, Chief Growth Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements within the meaning of the safe harbor provisions of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. Please refer to our SEC filings, including our most recent Form 10-K and 10-Q, for a discussion of the factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from these statements.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Michael.

Michael Thompson (CEO):
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. We are pleased to report our results for Q3 2024. We delivered strong performance despite ongoing macroeconomic headwinds and inflationary pressures in the Food & Beverage sector.

Today, I'll be focusing on four key areas: the impact of input cost inflation and supply chain disruptions, gross margin analysis including drivers and trends, EPS guidance and key assumptions, and our discussion of pricing actions and revenue growth management strategies.

First, regarding the impact of input cost inflation and supply chain disruptions: We've faced significant pressures but mitigated them through strategic pricing, hedging, and supply chain resilience measures.

Second, concerning gross margin analysis: drivers and trends: Our margins expanded meaningfully year-over-year, driven by pricing power, productivity gains, and favorable mix shifts.

Third, in terms of EPS guidance and key assumptions: We're on track with our full-year outlook, reflecting solid organic growth and disciplined cost management.

Finally, looking at our discussion of pricing actions and revenue growth management strategies: These have been instrumental in driving organic revenue growth ahead of expectations.

Overall, we are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah to provide more detail on our financial results.

Sarah Jenkins (CFO):
Thank you, Michael. As Michael mentioned, we achieved solid results in Q3 2024. Net sales were $6.8 billion, representing a 7.2% increase year-over-year. Gross margin was 41.8%, impacted by input cost inflation but bolstered by pricing and productivity. Operating income was $950 million, and diluted earnings per share were $1.35. We are managing our costs effectively and continue to invest in key growth initiatives.

Our balance sheet remains strong with $2.1 billion in cash and marketable securities. We are committed to returning value to shareholders through our quarterly dividend and $500 million in share repurchases year-to-date under our $1 billion authorization.

For the full year, we are reaffirming our guidance for adjusted EPS of $4.55 to $4.75.

Before we open the line for questions, let me dive deeper into the four key areas Michael highlighted, starting with the impact of input cost inflation and supply chain disruptions. Good morning again, everyone. As many of you know, the Food & Beverage sector has been navigating a perfect storm since early 2022, driven by geopolitical tensions, adverse weather patterns, and lingering post-pandemic logistics bottlenecks. For Global Foods Inc., these pressures resulted in an 11.8% year-over-year increase in our cost of goods sold, or COGS, compressing our adjusted gross margin by 210 basis points to 41.8%—our strongest resilience in recent quarters despite the challenges.

Let me break this down systematically. Input cost inflation accounted for roughly 70% of the COGS delta. Commodity prices across our portfolio—spanning beverages, snacks, and dairy—have surged due to structural supply constraints. For example, grains like wheat futures on the Chicago Mercantile Exchange spiked 28% year-to-date, largely from the Russia-Ukraine conflict disrupting Black Sea exports, which represent 25% of global supply. This has cascaded into our bakery and cereal categories, where wheat and corn inputs rose 22% and 19%, respectively. We've seen similar dynamics in edible oils; palm oil, critical for our snack coatings, jumped 15% amid Indonesian export curbs and El Niño-related yield shortfalls in Southeast Asia.

Dairy proteins tell an even starker story. Global milk powder prices climbed 18% on the Global Dairy Trade auction index, fueled by European heatwaves slashing production by 5-7% in key basins like Bavaria and Normandy. For our yogurt and cheese lines—our refrigerated segment, which comprises 22% of net sales—we faced a 16% uplift in skim milk powder costs. Sugar and cocoa haven't been immune either; cocoa beans hit all-time highs at $4,200 per metric ton on ICE futures, up 42% year-over-year from West African crop failures, pressuring our chocolate confectionery margins.

Packaging and non-food inputs exacerbated this. Aluminum for beverage cans rose 14% due to energy surcharges in smelters from the Pacific Northwest to Europe, while PET resin for bottles increased 12% amid ethylene cracker outages in the U.S. Gulf Coast. Labor inflation added another layer—our frontline manufacturing wages rose 9% amid a 3.8% unemployment rate tightening the pool, echoing trends at peers like Tyson Foods. Energy costs, tied to natural gas benchmarks, surged 25% in North America, inflating our steam and refrigeration expenses by 8%.

Regionally, the picture varies. In North America, which drives 55% of our revenue, COGS inflation landed at 12.5%, buffered somewhat by our hedging but hit hard by West Coast port strikes delaying container throughput by 20-30 days. Europe, at 25% of sales, saw a 15.2% COGS hike due to the EU's REPowerEU plan spiking natural gas to €80 per MWh and Red Sea disruptions rerouting shipments via the Cape of Good Hope, adding 15-20% to ocean freight from Asia. APAC, our growth engine at 20% of sales, moderated to 9.8% inflation thanks to localized sourcing in India and Vietnam, though avian flu outbreaks in China disrupted poultry inputs for our ready meals by 10%.

Shifting to supply chain disruptions, these amplified inflation by creating scarcity premiums and forcing air freight premiums—up 40% in spots. Our on-time delivery rate dipped to 87% from 96% a year ago, per our SCOR model metrics, leading to $45 million in lost sales from stockouts in high-velocity SKUs like our flagship carbonated soft drinks and salty snacks. Container rates on the Asia-U.S. lane peaked at $5,200 per FEU in Q1 before easing to $3,800, but trucking spot rates in the U.S. Midwest rose 18% due to ELD mandates and driver shortages. We've modeled this via our supply chain dashboard, showing a 14% effective freight cost increase, with intermodal shifts from truck-to-rail yielding only partial relief.

Crucially, our strategic response has mitigated what could have been a 400-plus basis point gross margin hit. First, pricing discipline: we executed three waves of list price increases totaling 8.5% across the portfolio, with 85% pass-through on elastic categories like beverages, recovering 60% of inflation. Average selling prices rose 7.2% year-over-year, outpacing category averages per Nielsen data.

On hedging, our commodities program—covering 65% of 2025 grain and dairy needs—locked in floors at pre-inflation levels via CBOT futures and OTC swaps, shielding $220 million in exposure. We've expanded this to 40% on cocoa and oils, partnering with firms like StoneX for dynamic collars that cap upside at 10% over spot.

Supply chain resilience is our North Star. We've diversified suppliers—reducing single-source dependency from 18% to 9% of inputs—sourcing wheat from the U.S. Plains and Australia instead of just Ukraine-adjacent routes. Nearshoring initiatives include a new dairy processing JV in Mexico, cutting LATAM lead times by 25%, and dual-sourcing PET from U.S. Gulf producers to bypass Asia. Inventory optimization via AI-driven demand sensing from Blue Yonder has trimmed safety stock by 12% while boosting service levels to 92%.

Technically, we're rolling out Industry 4.0 upgrades: predictive maintenance on our 45 high-speed lines using Siemens MindSphere IoT has lifted overall equipment effectiveness, or OEE, by 3 points to 88%, yielding $30 million in savings. Yield improvement programs in snacks—targeting 1-2% gains via precision dosing—have offset 15% of packaging inflation. SKU rationalization culled 12% of our 2,500-item portfolio, focusing on 80/20 winners like low-sugar beverages amid health trends.

Looking forward, we expect input inflation to moderate to 4-6% in FY2025 as harvests normalize—USDA projects a 5% wheat rebound—and supply chains stabilize with new capacity like the Panama Canal expansions. Freight should ease another 10-15% per Drewry indices. That said, we're not complacent; our $150 million capex plan includes vertical integration via a U.S. corn milling acquisition and blockchain traceability with IBM Food Trust to preempt disruptions.

In sum, while input inflation and disruptions shaved 80 basis points off adjusted EBITDA margins to 14.2%, our proactive playbook positions us for 100-plus basis points expansion next year. We're outperforming peers—our total shareholder return is up 8% year-to-date versus the XLP's flat performance—and remain committed to 12-15% organic growth.

Next, let's turn to gross margin analysis: drivers and trends. Our gross margin performance continues to be a standout story for the quarter and reflects the resilience of our Food & Beverage portfolio amid a volatile macro environment. Gross margin is a critical leading indicator for our operating leverage, where commodity volatility, supply chain disruptions, and shifting consumer preferences can swing margins by hundreds of basis points quarter-over-quarter.

For Q3, we delivered a consolidated gross margin of 42.5%, up 130 basis points year-over-year from 41.2% and 50 basis points sequentially from Q2's 42.0%. This marks our third consecutive quarter of gross margin expansion, bringing our trailing 12-month margin to 42.1%, the highest in five years and ahead of the industry average of around 38-40% as reported by peers like Mondelez and Hershey. This puts us on track for full-year gross margin guidance of 42.0-42.5%, assuming no further escalation in key input costs.

Using our standard margin bridge framework, refined post our SAP S/4HANA ERP rollout last year for more granular visibility into COGS components, here are the key drivers.

Pricing and revenue management contributed 220 basis points year-over-year. Pricing remains our most powerful lever. We implemented targeted list price increases averaging 5.2% across the portfolio, with higher hikes—up to 8%—on high-elasticity categories like carbonated soft drinks and salty snacks, where we saw minimal volume pushback. Average selling price grew 6.1% year-over-year, driven by premiumization trends. For instance, our NutriBoost functional beverage line, now 15% of beverage segment revenue, commanded a 25% ASP premium over standard SKUs, fueled by clean-label formulations with natural sweeteners amid consumer shifts away from high-fructose corn syrup. Regionally, North America saw 7.2% ASP growth thanks to strong pricing power in retail channels, while Europe lagged at 3.8% due to softer private-label competition from discounters like Aldi and Lidl.

Input cost inflation was a headwind of 80 basis points year-over-year. Headwinds here were manageable but persistent, primarily from cocoa and dairy. Global cocoa prices surged 45% year-over-year to over $10,000 per metric ton, per Bloomberg data, due to poor harvests in Côte d'Ivoire and Ghana—echoing the supply shocks that hit Hershey and Mondelez last year. This pressured our chocolate-coated snacks, which represent 12% of snacks segment COGS. Dairy costs rose 12% on stronger global demand and EU milk production constraints from avian flu outbreaks. We mitigated about 60% of this through hedging: our Q3 hedge book covered 70% of FY2024 cocoa needs at $7,200 per metric ton, locking in savings of $15 million. Positively, wheat and corn stabilized post-Ukraine war peaks, down 5% quarter-over-quarter, benefiting our bakery division. Overall input inflation was 4.2%, below the industry's 6-7% as per IRI data.

Volume and mix shift added 60 basis points year-over-year. Favorable mix provided tailwinds as consumers traded up to premium and health-focused products. Premium and better-for-you SKUs grew to 28% of total revenue, up from 22% year-over-year, including our plant-based GreenWave yogurt alternatives and low-sugar gummies. These carry gross margins 500-700 basis points above the portfolio average. Volume was flat overall, but mix benefits offset this: snacks mix improved 2.2 points from strength in protein bars, while beverages saw headwinds from declining soda volumes, down 3% in North America club channels.

Supply chain and productivity initiatives contributed 130 basis points year-over-year on a cumulative basis. Our MarginMax program, now in Phase 2, delivered $28 million in Q3 savings through yield improvements—AI-driven manufacturing optimization at our Ohio and Mexico plants boosted conversion yields by 1.8% on snacks, reducing waste from 3.2% to 1.4%. Sourcing optimization via our new almond co-op in California cut nut costs 15%, insulating us from California's drought-driven price spikes. Freight and packaging efficiencies: inbound ocean freight rates fell 20% quarter-over-quarter post-Red Sea disruptions, and our switch to 30% recycled PET in bottles saved $8 million while meeting EU sustainability mandates. Regionally, APAC margins expanded 250 basis points to 44.2% on localized sourcing in Indonesia for palm oil, down 10% amid oversupply, versus Latin America's flat 39.5% due to Brazil sugar volatility.

Looking at trends, we're seeing a multi-year inflection: post-COVID supply chain scarring has de-rated F&B gross margins from 2022 peaks, but winners like us are pulling away via pricing discipline and tech. Our margins now exceed pre-pandemic levels from FY2019 at 40.8%, driven by a structural shift to premiumization—McKinsey estimates this could add 200-300 basis points industry-wide by 2027.

Strategically, we're doubling down on resilience with $150 million in capex for FY2025 for automation, including robotic palletizers at three plants to cut labor COGS by 15%. Sustainable sourcing commitments include 50% cage-free eggs by year-end 2024 and regenerative agriculture for 30% of grains, hedging climate risks while qualifying for retailer rebates like Walmart's Gigaton program. Risks to watch: El Niño forecasts could reflate cocoa and dairy into Q4; we're 80% hedged. Europe inflation may cap further pricing.

Moving to our EPS guidance and key assumptions for the full year FY2024. We're reaffirming adjusted EPS of $4.55 to $4.75 per diluted share, implying 8% to 13% growth over FY2023's $4.20. This range reflects core business momentum, strategic execution, and conservatism around exogenous factors like foreign exchange and commodity volatility. It embeds about $0.15 of dilution from our recent acquisition of Horizon Plant-Based Dairy, which closed in Q2 and is already tracking toward 10% ROIC in Year 1 through synergies in our shared cold-chain distribution network.

Breaking it down by key assumptions across the P&L, with a focus on our beverages like the flagship AquaSparkle hydration line and ZeroCal energy drinks, alongside snacks including protein-packed NutriBars and reformulated savory crisps.

Revenue outlook calls for organic growth of 6% to 8%, with total net sales flat to plus 2%. Organic growth drivers include 3-4% pricing actions and 3-4% volume/mix tailwinds. Pricing will be disciplined, with North America seeing modest 2-3% increases on premium SKUs like our reformulated low-sugar sodas, while emerging markets like Latin America and APAC absorb fuller inflation pass-through at 5-6%. Volume/mix benefits from our health and wellness pivot: plant-based beverages now represent 15% of our beverage portfolio, up from 10% last year, with double-digit velocity gains in almond and oat milks, mirroring trends at peers like Danone and Chobani. In snacks, we're targeting average unit volume uplift through better in-store merchandising and e-commerce basket expansion—our average basket size in snacks has grown 12% year-over-year via cross-promotions with beverages.

Regionally, North America, 55% of sales, expects 4-6% organic growth from resilient at-home demand and premiumization in hydration, like plus 15% in functional waters. EMEA, 20%, 7-9% from stronger pricing power amid Eurozone recovery and sustainability premiums on recyclable packaging boosting share in UK and Iberia. APAC and Latin America, 25%, 8-10% with double-digit volume in Indonesia and Brazil via affordable sachets and local flavor innovations like mango-ginger energy shots. Headwinds: total net sales growth factors in minus 3% FX impact, primarily from ARS and TRY devaluation, and minus 1% from M&A and divestiture drag as we've pruned 20% of low-velocity legacy items to focus on high-margin winners.

Gross margin expansion of 150-200 basis points to 39.0-39.5%, up from 37.5% in FY2023, driven by supply chain productivity gains of 250 basis points offset partially by input inflation. Commodity costs: hedged wheat and corn at plus 3-5% year-over-year below USDA forecasts, but unhedged cocoa and sugar up 10-12% due to West African disruptions—we've mitigated via forward contracts covering 70% of needs through Q4. Dairy alternatives stable as oat supply chains optimize. Technical initiatives: full rollout of our AI-powered demand sensing platform has reduced waste by 8% and improved fill rates to 98%. Automation upgrades at our top five plants deliver 4% COGS savings. Freight normalization saves another 50 basis points. Packaging innovation: 30% shift to mono-material rPET bottles cuts resin costs by 7%, aligning with regulations.

Operating expenses: SG&A as a percent of sales at 28.0-28.5%, down 50 basis points, with $0.25 per share in expense leverage through zero-based budgeting and digital transformation. Marketing spend holds at 12% of sales, skewed toward performance media with ROAS over 5x on TikTok and Amazon for Gen Z campaigns, and shopper activation in channels like Walmart and Amazon Fresh. R&D at 2.5% of sales funds pipeline hits like Q4 launch of collagen-infused protein waters targeting 5% beverage mix by FY2025 and upcycled ingredient snacks to tap the $100 billion-plus regenerative ag market. G&A efficiencies from SAP S/4HANA yield $40 million annualized savings.

Other assumptions: operating income growth 10-14% to $1.8-1.9 billion, with margin expansion to 16.5-17.0%. Net interest expense $120 million on Horizon debt at 4.5% blended rate; effective tax rate steady at 23.5% with U.S. R&D credits and Irish IP structuring. Average diluted shares 425 million after $300 million buybacks. Capex disciplined at 3.0-3.2% of sales, $650-700 million, prioritized for precision fermentation for alt-proteins and solar microgrids at Latin America facilities.

Strategically, this underscores our Health Forward, Profit Strong framework: 60% of innovation budget on nutrient-dense, low-sugar products to capture the 7% CAGR in functional F&B per NielsenIQ. We're accelerating portfolio shaping—expect another $200 million in divestitures of low-teens margin legacy brands by mid-FY2025, recycling proceeds into bolt-ons.

Key risks: consumer downtrading if U.S. unemployment ticks above 4.2%, softening value-pack velocity 2-3%; we've stress-tested with dynamic pricing. Geopolitical supply issues like Red Sea adding 1-2% to freight, countered by nearshoring 20% of APAC sourcing to Mexico. Regulatory like soda tax expansions or EU labeling pressuring volumes 1%, offset by premium products.

Finally, on pricing actions and revenue growth management strategies, these were pivotal in delivering our organic revenue growth of 5.2% this quarter, ahead of our guided range of 4 to 5%. This marks the third consecutive quarter of positive organic growth amid persistent commodity inflation, shifting consumer behaviors, and heightened competition from CPG giants like PepsiCo and rising private label penetration.

We executed targeted price increases averaging 6.8% across our portfolio since the beginning of the year, contributing 4.5 percentage points to organic revenue growth. This was a granular, SKU-level strategy informed by our advanced revenue growth management platform, powered by AI-driven elasticity modeling. We segmented by category, channel, and geography to optimize recovery and elasticity.

In beverages, 45% of net revenues, pricing was up 7.2%, driven by carryover from Q1 increases on core brands like NutriCola and Sparkle energy drinks. We saw positive price-mix elasticity of 1.2x, with volumes holding up thanks to premiumization—we shifted 12% of volume to zero-sugar and functional variants like NutriCola Zero+ with electrolytes, commanding 25-30% premium. IRI scan data shows functional beverages growing 14% year-over-year in North America.

Food segment—snacks and dairy at 35% of revenues—saw 5.9% pricing, with 4-6% hikes on indulgent items like Crunchy Bites amid cocoa up 45% year-to-date. On value dairy like Everyday Yogurt multipacks, we limited to 2-3% and layered everyday low pricing to defend against private labels, which gained 2.1 points per Nielsen.

Our RGM framework encompasses pricing discipline, portfolio optimization, innovation velocity, and trade spend efficiency. Mix management added 1.1 points from 8% uplift in premium mix—from OatBev plant-based milk at 15% of dairy to high-protein snacks. Volumes down 0.4% overall, but e-commerce up 22% as consumers upgraded online.

North America, 55% of revenues, pricing delivered 5.2 points, bolstered by resilient wallets and leadership in non-alcoholic beverages. Volumes dipped 0.8% from promotion stacking, but we optimized trade spend down 120 basis points to 22% via zero-based budgeting and AI-forecasted ROIs.

EMEA, 20%, pricing at 4.1 points amid inflation-weary shoppers—EU food CPI plus 5.2%. Volumes fell 2.3%, countered by value packs in France preserving share versus Danone. Innovation like stevia-sweetened NutriCola Q4 rollout projected at €50 million incremental at 15% margins.

APAC and LATAM, 25%, tempered pricing at 3.9 points fueled 4.2% volume expansion in India and Brazil with dynamic pricing and retailer partnerships reducing trade leakages 15%.

Forward, pricing actions 4-5% for FY2024 on 200-plus low-elasticity SKUs, investing $250 million in innovation for sustainable packaging and clean-label to tap health trends. Piloting blockchain for cocoa and dairy to mitigate volatility.

In summary, these strategies safeguarded margins—expanding gross margin by 210 basis points to 42.3%—and position us for 4-6% organic growth through FY2025.

Now, let's open the call for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, at this time we will begin the question-and-answer session. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Emily Carter with JPMorgan. Please proceed.

Emily Carter (JPMorgan):
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of input cost inflation on your business?

Michael Thompson (CEO):
Thanks, Emily. As Sarah outlined in detail, input cost inflation has been a significant headwind, up 11.8% in COGS, but our hedging covering 65% of key commodities and 8.5% pricing actions have recovered the majority. We're seeing moderation ahead and remain positioned for margin expansion.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Rossi with Barclays. Please proceed.

Mike Rossi (Barclays):
What are your plans for the new NutriBoost functional beverage line and what is the expected revenue impact?

Lisa Chen (Chief Growth Officer):
Thanks, Mike. The NutriBoost line is a cornerstone of our premiumization strategy, now 15% of beverage revenue with a 25% ASP premium from clean-label features. We're planning expanded distribution into club channels and e-commerce, expecting $150 million in incremental revenue next year, driving 3-4 points of volume/mix growth.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sarah Lee with Morgan Stanley. Please proceed.

Sarah Lee (Morgan Stanley):
How are you managing supply chain disruptions?

Raj Patel (Chief Supply Chain Officer):
Good question, Sarah. We've diversified suppliers to cut single-source risk to 9%, nearshored dairy to Mexico reducing lead times 25%, and deployed AI demand sensing for 92% service levels. OEE is up to 88% via IoT, and we're investing in blockchain for traceability—on-time delivery rebounding to 92% expected by year-end.

Operator:
Our last question comes from David Kim with Citi. Please proceed.

David Kim (Citi):
What is your outlook for the rest of the year?

Sarah Jenkins (CFO):
Thanks, David. We're reaffirming full-year EPS of $4.55 to $4.75, with 6-8% organic growth from pricing and health-focused mix. Margins expand to 39-39.5% on productivity, despite moderating inflation. Risks like FX are baked in, but upside from innovation and synergies positions us at the midpoint or better.

Operator:
I would now like to turn the call back over to Michael Thompson for closing remarks.

Michael Thompson (CEO):
Thank you for your questions and your continued interest in Global Foods Inc. We are focused on executing our strategy and delivering strong results. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.

Mitigated via 8.5% pricing (60% inflation recovery), 65% hedging on grains/dairy, supplier diversification (single-source to 9%), nearshoring, AI inventory optimization, Industry 4.0 (OEE to 88%). Expect 4-6% inflation moderation in FY2025.

Trends: 3rd straight quarter expansion, FY guide 42.0-42.5%; structural premiumization, capex for automation/sustainability.

Positive elasticity 1.2x, mix +1.1 pts (premium to 8% uplift). RGM framework: pricing discipline, portfolio optimization (SKU cull), innovation, trade spend efficiency (-120 bps).
